titleEn: Eat in Your Chair, Right to the End!

pages.text: "A butterfly outside!" Careless Duri jumped off the chair carrying a plate. Lunch noodles steamed on the long window table. Only Duri's chair was empty.
"I will finish quickly and go outside first!" Duri wandered between window and door, eating a bite each time. Noodle strands fell on the floor.
Mio, who wanted to do everything alone, stayed in their chair to eat. "Duri, your plate is wobbling." Duri tugged the purple neckerchief knot and giggled.
Duri turned sharply at the door—and the plate slipped. Splat! Noodles spilled all over the floor.
Still seated, Mio said, "I will finish right here. Eat in your chair, right to the end!" Duri looked down at the spilled noodles.
Duri wiped the floor with a cloth. Fresh noodles arrived, but now there was no steam. They had cooled and tasted bland.
Meanwhile, the friends finished and went outside. Laughter came through the window. Alone at the table, Duri ate cold noodles.
Teacher Bau sat opposite and set down a bowl. "I always sit in a chair to eat too. Standing leaves only half the taste." Duri pulled in their chair and sat.
At lunch the next day, a butterfly fluttered past again. Duri kept their bottom firmly in the chair. "One, plate on the table! Two, both feet on the floor! Three, get up when the bowl is empty!"
Duri held up an empty bowl and ran outside first. Teacher Bau stroked their back. Staying seated kept noodles warm and left time for the yard. "Butterfly, wait! Eat in your chair, right to the end!"
